Hull City manager Sergej Jakirović has eased concerns over Semi Ajayi’s fitness after revealing that the Nigerian defender was among two players withdrawn with cramps during Saturday’s 1-0 defeat to Arsenal. Ajayi, who delivered a solid defensive performance at the Emirates Stadium, was replaced in the 69th minute, raising concerns over his availability for Nigeria’s upcoming international engagements. However, Jakirović clarified after the encounter that the defender’s withdrawal was not caused by a serious injury. “It’s very difficult; we had two players with cramps, and also we tried to close the midfield zone today because Arsenal are doing everything to overload the midfield, and it is not easy to control,” the Hull manager told Sky Sports. The clarification was reinforced by reports from Hull, which stated that Ajayi was taken off because of cramp and was not dealing with anything more serious. His withdrawal came three minutes before Martin Ødegaard scored the only goal of the game in the 72nd minute, following a save by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Ajayi’s fitness will be welcome news for Nigeria as the Super Eagles prepare for their forthcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixtures against Tanzania. The defender has been an important option in Nigeria’s backline, and his availability will be valuable as the team continues preparations for the international assignment.
